name: Jehoshaphat
bio:
Jehoshaphat was Asa's son, who succeeded him as king of Judah after Asa's forty-one-year reign ended and he was buried with his ancestors in the City of David (1 Kings 15:24).

Chronicles opens his reign with its own distinctive material. Jehoshaphat fortified Judah's cities, sought the LORD as David had rather than following Israel's ways, and removed the high places and Asherah poles, so the LORD established the kingdom firmly in his hand and gave him great riches and honor. In his third year, he sent officials, Levites, and priests throughout Judah's towns carrying the Book of the Law to teach the people, and as a result the fear of the LORD fell on the surrounding kingdoms, none of whom made war against him; the Philistines brought him tribute and the Arabians brought flocks, and he grew exceedingly great, fortifying store cities and maintaining a vast standing army across Judah and Benjamin (2 Chronicles 17:1-19).

## 📖 Core Story: Ramoth Gilead, and a Faithful Reign

Jehoshaphat allied with Ahab against Syria, agreeing to join the attack on Ramoth Gilead with his own people and horses, but first asked Ahab to seek the LORD's word. When four hundred court prophets promised victory, Jehoshaphat pressed for a true prophet of the LORD, leading to Micaiah being summoned and, alone among them, prophesying Ahab's death. Jehoshaphat went into battle anyway at Ahab's side wearing his royal robes while Ahab disguised himself, and when the Syrian chariot captains mistook Jehoshaphat for the king of Israel and converged on him, he cried out and was spared once they realized their error — while Ahab, disguised, was struck by a stray arrow and died (1 Kings 22:1-35).

When Jehoshaphat returned home safely, the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and asked how he could help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD, warning that the LORD's wrath was on him for it — though he also commended Jehoshaphat for removing the Asherah poles and seeking God wholeheartedly. Jehoshaphat then toured the land from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, turning the people back to the LORD, and appointed judges in every fortified city of Judah, charging them to judge not for man but for the LORD, fearing him and showing no partiality or taking bribes. In Jerusalem he also established a central court of Levites, priests, and family leaders to handle disputes referred from the towns, placing Amariah the chief priest over matters of the LORD and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, head of the tribe of Judah, over the king's matters, and charging them all to act courageously and faithfully (2 Chronicles 19:1-11).

Jehoshaphat began to reign over Judah at thirty-five, ruling twenty-five years in Jerusalem; Scripture commends him for walking in his father Asa's righteous ways, doing right in the LORD's eyes, though the high places remained and the people still sacrificed there. He finished removing the remaining shrine prostitutes his father had left, made peace with the king of Israel, and built ships of Tharshish to sail for gold from Ophir, though they wrecked at Ezion Geber before ever sailing; he refused Ahaziah son of Ahab's request to send servants along on that venture (1 Kings 22:41-50).

## 📖 Core Story: Allied Against Moab

When Jehoram of Israel asked Jehoshaphat to join him against the rebelling Mesha, king of Moab, Jehoshaphat agreed at once, bringing his people and horses as he had for Ahab before. The allied march through the wilderness of Edom left the combined armies without water, and it was Jehoshaphat who insisted on consulting a true prophet of the LORD, leading them to Elisha. Elisha prophesied the valley would fill with water and Moab would be delivered into their hands despite having no rain or wind — and both came true, water filling the land and the Moabite army routed, though Mesha's sacrifice of his own son at Kir Hareseth finally drove the allied kings to withdraw (2 Kings 3:1-27).
